newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JACKSON FIRST TO PRAISE JOHNSON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JACKSON FIRST TO PRAISE JOHNSON.

text.p: World record holder Colin Jackson was the first to congratulate Allen Johnson after the American beat him to the world 110 metres hurdles title on Thursday.
"I ran the time I expected but it wasn't enough, Allen was fantastic," said Jackson, who took the silver medal in 13.05 seconds.

Their mutual admiration for one another continued when Johnson, who won the title for the second successive time in 12.93 seconds, just two-hundredths of a second outside Jackson's four-year-old world record, was equally complimentary about the Briton.

"If I had made the smallest little mistake tonight, Colin would have shot right by me. He is a fantastic starter so I had to get an even better start and get to the first hurdle before he did," Johnson said.
"Colin has been running so well I knew I couldn't make any mistakes. I had to run to win, not for the world record.
"I kind of played it safe just a little bit so I could stay in front of him and be number one."
Johnson said he had been inspired by a biblical message from his training partner Melissa Morrison.
Morrison wrote on a sticky label which he placed on his singlet above his heart: "I can do everything through him. He who gives me strength."
He certainly needed strength of mind and body to win on Thursday, especially as Jackson, who has endured a miserable couple of years hampered by injury, ran outstandingly well in the earlier rounds.
"It's wonderful to be back, its very important that I am still able to show I am one of the best in the world. I think Allen and I both can run under 12.90 this season," Jackson said.
Johnson also indicated the world record could fall in the next few weeks.
"Once we get back on the circuit, I'll be able to take chances, I won't have to play it safe."
